claims.text: A refractory high-entropy alloy containing substantial fractions of Nb and Ti can become superconducting at cryogenic temperatures.
Nb supports electron–phonon coupling conducive to Cooper-pair formation.
Ti supports electron–phonon coupling conducive to Cooper-pair formation.
The proposed cast, near-equiatomic Nb–Ti–Ta–Zr-type refractory HEA can be homogeneous.
The proposed refractory HEA can possess a stable BCC or otherwise single-phase microstructure at ambient temperature.
A single-phase BCC microstructure minimizes scattering from grain boundaries and impurities.
Reduced scattering in the single-phase BCC microstructure mediates coherent electron transport.
Electron–phonon coupling in the Nb/Ti-rich alloy leads to Cooper-pair formation below a critical temperature.
Cooper-pair formation in this alloy results in zero electrical resistance.
The superconducting state of this alloy produces magnetic-flux expulsion through the Meissner effect.
The alloy should undergo a superconducting transition at a temperature of approximately 20 K or lower.
At ambient temperature, the proposed alloy is a normal metal with finite electrical resistance.
At ambient temperature, the proposed alloy has standard magnetic susceptibility rather than a superconducting magnetic response.
Superconductivity requires the alloy to retain a homogeneous, single-phase microstructure with minimal defects.
Secondary phases or additional defects may inhibit or suppress superconductivity in the alloy.
